title: Semantic-Preserving KV Cache Compression for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
one_line_claim: Compresses KV cache by grouping tokens into semantic chunks and selecting top-k chunks via attention scores, with layer-wise index reuse for efficiency.
method_summary: ChunkKV groups consecutive tokens into chunks and computes chunk-level attention scores from token attention weights. Top-k chunks are selected and concatenated to form the compressed cache. Layer-wise index reuse reuses chunk indices across transformer layers to avoid redundant computation.

key_findings.finding: ChunkKV achieves 4.5x compression while maintaining 99% of full-context quality on GSM8K.
key_findings.quote: ChunkKV achieves 4.5x compression ratio while maintaining 99% of full-context quality on GSM8K

key_findings.finding: Layer-wise index reuse improves throughput by 26.5% compared to token-by-token recomputation.
key_findings.quote: Our layer-wise index reuse mechanism achieves 26.5% throughput improvement

key_findings.finding: ChunkKV maintains quality across LongBench (BLEU), NIAH (up to 32K context), and JailbreakV while achieving 4-8x compression.
key_findings.quote: ChunkKV maintains quality across LongBench (BLEU), NIAH (up to 32K context), and JailbreakV while achieving 4-8x compression

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression efficiency in long-context LLM inference and aim to enable practical deployment without catastrophic failures.
differs_on: ChunkKV uses semantic chunking and attention-based chunk selection; HERALD uses per-token logit features to predict failures before they occur.
ChunkKV is a compression method; HERALD is a failure predictor that treats any compressor as a black box.
ChunkKV operates at compression time; HERALD monitors signals during generation to forecast H tokens ahead.
